levels.name: Beginner
levels.description: Start with one Latin root and notice how prefixes shape meaning.

module.title: Writing roots
module.summary: Meet scribere and words formed from the Latin ‘to write’ root.

lesson.title: Scribere: the writing family
lesson.introduction: Explore describe, inscription, manuscript, and transcript. Each connects to Latin scribere through a different word form or prefix.

questions.prompt: Which Latin verb is at the heart of describe?
questions.explanation: Describe comes from Latin describere, from de- + scribere.

questions.prompt: In inscription, what does the Latin prefix in- contribute?
questions.explanation: Here in- means ‘in’ or ‘on’, as in writing on a surface.

questions.prompt: What does manu mean in the Latin expression behind manuscript?
questions.explanation: Manu is the ablative form of manus, ‘hand’; scriptus means ‘written’.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.description: Compare prefixes and related forms in a second Latin word family.

module.title: Movement and direction
module.summary: Follow portare through words about carrying in, out, across, and from place to place.

lesson.title: Portare: carrying across
lesson.introduction: The Latin verb portare means ‘to carry’. Prefixes and later Latin forms shape the English words in this family.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix trans- mean in transport?
questions.explanation: Latin trans- means ‘across’ or ‘beyond’; transportare meant to carry across.

questions.prompt: Which Latin verb contributes the ‘carry’ element in import?
questions.explanation: Import comes from Latin importare, formed with in- and portare.

questions.prompt: Portable reached English through later forms of which Latin verb?
questions.explanation: Portable comes through French portable and Late Latin portabilis, from Latin portare.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.description: Read more closely: distinguish shared roots, prefixes, and historical word forms.

module.title: Morphology in context
module.summary: Compare the formation paths of familiar words without relying on spelling alone.

lesson.title: Forms and pathways
lesson.introduction: The same historical root can reach English through different Latin forms. Identify the specific route and avoid treating every similar spelling as the same morpheme.

questions.prompt: Which part of manuscript contributes the meaning ‘by hand’?
questions.explanation: Manu comes from manus, ‘hand’; scriptus is a form of scribere, ‘to write’.

questions.prompt: Transcript is based on a Latin form of which verb?
questions.explanation: Transcript comes from Latin transcriptum, the neuter past participle of transcribere.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes portable’s connection to portare?
questions.explanation: Portable came through French and Late Latin portabilis, which is from portare.
choices: It is root-related through later forms, not a direct English prefix + root construction.
It is a direct English compound of port + able.
It shares only a similar spelling, with no historical link.
